tagline: Presentations and infographics that a reader clicks through rather than watches.
verdictSummary: Visme's difference from a general design tool is that its output is interactive: hotspots that reveal detail, tabs, click-through steps, embedded charts. Emitting that as a self-contained HTML document is a real project — the interaction model has to be authored visually and then survive export with keyboard access and no external dependencies. It is a few days of work, and what you cannot rebuild is the reason people choose Visme, which is thousands of templates that already look designed.
coreLoopDIY: Compose a document from themed blocks with hotspots and click-through interactions, and export a single self-contained HTML file that works offline.
whatYouLose: the template library and the stock asset collections
the view analytics on a shared document
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the templates are the product for most of its users, and a well-built interactive editor with three themes still produces something that looks homemade next to a designed template.
notes: Interactive HTML output is the angle: the catalogue's other design entries produce static images, print-quality decks or data-driven posters.
prompt:
Build an interactive document composer whose output is a single self-contained HTML file.

Document model: a sequence of blocks in a fixed-width column, or a slide-per-screen mode for presentation output. Block types: heading, text, image, chart, table, quote, and three interactive types described below.

Interactive blocks, which are the point of this build:

- Hotspot image: an image with markers placed on it, each revealing a small panel of text on click or keyboard focus. Placement is by percentage of the image, so it survives resizing.
- Tabs: a set of labelled panels, one visible at a time.
- Reveal sequence: a set of steps shown one at a time with previous and next controls, for walking a reader through a process.

Accessibility is not optional here, because interactivity is where documents usually become unusable. Every interactive element must be a real button or a tab pattern with correct ARIA roles, operable by keyboard, with visible focus and a sensible tab order. Test with the keyboard only before considering any interaction finished.

Charts: generated from pasted CSV, styled from the theme tokens, rendered as inline SVG with a data table alternative available so the content is readable without the picture.

Theme: a token file with a type scale, palette, spacing and radius. Blocks consume tokens only.

Export, which is where the effort concentrates: a single HTML file with all CSS inlined, all JavaScript inlined and under a few kilobytes, images embedded as data URIs or written alongside as the user chooses, and fonts either embedded or falling back to system stacks. The file must open from a local disk with no network access and behave identically. That constraint is what makes the output shareable by email, and it should be tested with the network disabled.

Also export: a static PDF where every interactive block is flattened to its full content — every tab panel, every reveal step, every hotspot with its text — because a PDF that shows only the first tab is a broken document.

Storage: the document as JSON on disk with referenced assets, so it lives in a repository.

Out of scope: a template library, stock asset collections, real-time collaboration, hosted sharing and view analytics, and video or animated export.

faq.q: Can I export a Visme project?
faq.a: As PDF, PNG and sometimes HTML, none of which is an editable source. A project is rebuilt here, and the interactive parts in particular have to be re-authored since no export preserves them as structure.

faq.q: Why insist on a single self-contained file?
faq.a: Because that is what makes an interactive document shareable. A folder of assets breaks the moment it is emailed, and a hosted link stops working when you stop paying. One file that opens offline is the only form of interactive document that genuinely outlives the tool that made it.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing. Local editor, local export, no account and no keys. The output file is yours and has no dependency on anything.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Looking professional without a designer. Visme's library means a first attempt looks finished; an empty editor with three themes means a first attempt looks like a first attempt, and for a document meant to persuade somebody that is most of the value gone.
